html:
A city in northern Morocco, founded in 789 by Idris I, a descendant of the Prophet who had fled the Abbasids and founded the Idrisid dynasty. His son Idris II built a second town across the river in 809, and the two grew into one city.

Refugees made Fez. Families expelled from Córdoba in al-Andalus settled one bank, and families from Kairouan the other; the quarters still bear their names. A woman from the Kairouan community, Fatima al-Fihri, founded in 859 the mosque that became the University of al-Qarawiyyin, often called the oldest working university.

Fez was capital of Morocco under several dynasties, above all the Marinids in the 13th and 14th centuries, who added a new royal city beside the old. Its old walled medina, Fes el Bali, is a maze of thousands of lanes, among the largest car free urban areas in the world, with its famous leather tanneries. It is a World Heritage Site and was home for a time to Maimonides.
